extracted.intended_audience: progressive women readers and prospective contributors/subscribers to early-20th-century reformist magazines (e.g., The Forerunner)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit editorial criteria for pieces suited to The Forerunner and similar progressive periodicals: thematic alignment with social reform, preferred forms (fiction, essays, satire, poetry), tone (trenchant, didactic, concise), and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for The Forerunner (content and themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Forerunner carries Mrs. Gilman's best and newest work; her social philosophy, her verse, satire, fiction, ethical teaching, humor, and comment. It stands for Humanness in Women, and in Men; for better methods in Child-culture; for the Home that is no Workshop; for the New Ethics, the New Economics, the New World we are to make--are making."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces should align with social-reform themes and the magazine's philosophy; the publication targets readers who 'believe this world is a good place, easily made better.' It is explicitly not a 'popular magazine'—it meets the needs of a comparatively few, committed readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused, theme-driven criticism/review (example: Marriage as a Trade)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Her special matter in discussion is exactly given in the title, and she does not stray from her theme; but brings out, sharply and inescapably, the universal fact..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and critical essays are valued when they stay tightly on their central thesis, illuminate a broad truth from a specific vantage (here, the woman's view), and employ sharp, incisive language—'trenchant wit and penetrating satire'—to make points inescapable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel quality: strength, thrill, workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mary Jonston is a writer of good novels, strong, thrilling, excellent in workmanship..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction valued for strong plotting, emotional impact ('thrilling'), and careful craftsmanship. Literary skill and workmanship are emphasized as distinguishing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist/author practice: balance, intrinsic judgment, persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to an artist: '1. Live to your fullest development in all lines--and keep your health... 2. Do the work you think best, with all your might, accepting others' judgement only when it convinces yours. 3. Trying, always--that is, doing your best work, life long--is what allows those happy accidents. Keep on trying.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative practice rubric: maintain life/art balance and health; prioritize your own informed judgement about which work is best; persistently practice and keep producing to enable serendipitous successes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial features for The Englishwoman
rubrics_metrics.description: "The chief features will be: Articles dealing with the Women's Movement in England and other countries. Notes on parliamentary bills as affecting women and children. Articles on Women's Work in Professions and Trades. Sociological questions and their influence on the status of women. Stories, poems, scientific articles, and short plays. Criticisms of music, painting, sculpture, and current literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission/content rubric: accept pieces across reporting, analysis, sociology, creative writing and arts criticism, but with an emphasis on enfranchisement and impartial statement of facts; tone aimed at the 'cultured public' and 'moderate' persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial scope of The Common Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contains leaders and articles on political, social, legal and industrial matters affecting women, and is a complete record or the work done by the National Union for the enfranchisement of women."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should document and analyze political/organizational activity around women's enfranchisement; suitable for readers seeking authoritative records and political analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission and tone of The Progressive Woman
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Progressive Woman stands for a better race through the political and economic freedom of womankind. Its contributors are among the cleverest of the more advanced thinkers, and its readers endeavor to keep up with its writers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts advanced, forward-thinking political/economic argumentation; expects intellectually ambitious, progressive pieces that 'lead' readers rather than merely reflect mainstream positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted topics for Woman's Era
rubrics_metrics.description: "A World-wide Review With Original Articles on ECONOMICS, ETHICS, CIVICS, ARTS AND CRAFTS, MUSIC, LITERATURE, CLUB WORK, Etc."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial criterion: broad interdisciplinary coverage of civic, cultural, and educational topics aimed at inspiring American women; original articles across these domains are solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone/style for Up the Divide (voice and rhetorical energy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptors: 'Breezy, vigorous.' 'Brusher away of cobwebs.' 'Full of burning words.' 'Crisp and bold thoughts.' 'An eye-opener.' 'Charged with the gunpowder of progress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces should be lively, provocative, and rhetorically energetic—intended to invigorate readers and push progressive ideas; a distinctive, bold editorial voice is a criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political-issue focus for The Star
rubrics_metrics.description: "A WIDE-AWAKE, UP-TO-DATE PAPER FEARLESS, FRANK AND FREE. The First in the Land to Advocate Direct Legislation. Stands for Human Rights, including Votes for Women. Considers all Questions of Public Moment, such as Public Ownership, the Single Tax, the Tariff, etc."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts politically engaged journalism and commentary advocating direct legislation and broad human-rights issues; expects frankness and up-to-date coverage of public policy debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader-valued qualities: homogeneity, clarity, elevation from individual to systemic
rubrics_metrics.description: "Such a pleasure to read a homogeneous magazine... admires the way you take the individual problems of individual women, and by means of the individual problems lead these women into the larger view of life and into an understanding of the androcentric culture. 'Article on Socialism most concise, clearest and most convincing she has ever read.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorially prized attributes: coherent, thematically unified issues; clear, concise argumentation; pieces that use particular stories or problems to illuminate larger social structures and cultural critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable forms and serial publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first year comprises fourteen issues... In it is the Housekeeping novel--'What Diantha Did'... In it is also the Book About Men--'The Man-Made World, or Our Androcentric Culture.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazine accepts serialized novels and substantial thematic works; long-form fiction and multi-part treatments are suitable and may later be collected into bound volumes.
